question: What is the smallest deterministic evidence model that can distinguish insufficient longitudinal evidence from sufficient evidence to DESIGN a controlled canary, without turning observational correlation into a promotion decision?

options_considered.name: Fixed global sample threshold
options_considered.summary: Single threshold across all observations (e.g., 50 total records) regardless of class representation or policy consistency.
options_considered.tradeoffs: Too coarse; obscures class-specific absence; ignores policy drift and hash-chain corruption.

options_considered.name: Multi-dimensional deterministic readiness contract with per-advisory-class evaluation
options_considered.summary: Deterministic multi-gate evaluation combining journal integrity (hash-chain/sequence), policy consistency (zero fingerprint/version drift), observation quality (bounded UNKNOWN rate), and per-advisory-class occurrence/divergence thresholds.
options_considered.tradeoffs: Rigorous, fail-closed on integrity/drift, strictly limits output semantics to READY_FOR_CANARY_DESIGN without granting promotion or execution authority.

options_considered.name: Probabilistic Bayesian confidence model with arbitrary priors
options_considered.summary: Statistical inference attempting to estimate promotion likelihood without an intervention.
options_considered.tradeoffs: Violates KAD deterministic doctrine; pretends unexecuted counterfactuals provide causal empirical evidence.

rationale: Option B enforces multi-dimensional deterministic validation (integrity, policy consistency, quality, class-level counts) and strictly respects the epistemic invariant 'No causal claims without intervention'. Output states are limited to INSUFFICIENT_DATA, INVALID_EVIDENCE, POLICY_DRIFT, and READY_FOR_CANARY_DESIGN.
invariants: READY_FOR_CANARY_DESIGN authorizes experiment design only, never promotion or routing mutation.
Fail-closed on broken hash chain, sequence gaps, or policy fingerprint drift.
Synthetic test fixtures can never masquerade as live evidence.
